findings.title: No fallback/error handling when both userStorage and local credential provider fail
findings.body: createRecoveryCodesCredential() calls user.credentialManager().updateCredential() and if that returns false, falls back to recoveryCodeCredentialProvider.createCredential(). However there is no check of the return value of createCredential nor any indication to the caller whether credential creation succeeded (unlike createOTPCredential which returns a boolean). If both the user storage update and local creation fail silently (e.g. provider returns null), the required action (RecoveryAuthnCodesAction) will still call reqActionContext.success() unconditionally, leading to users believing recovery codes were saved when they were not.

findings.title: Unchecked raw List type used for recovery code comparisons
findings.body: In isValid(), generatedKeys is declared as a raw List (no generic type), and compared with input.getChallengeResponse() via key.equals(...). Since JsonSerialization.readValue deserializes JSON array elements that could be any type, this raises an unchecked-cast/type-safety concern and makes it brittle if the recovery code data format changes. This should use List<String> and verify hashed comparisons, consistent with RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.verifyRecoveryCodeInput used elsewhere, rather than ad hoc plain-text equality checking against raw codes (potential inconsistency with how codes are hashed/stored in the real implementation).

findings.title: generatedCodes passed to createRecoveryCodesCredential are raw strings, not re-validated against credentialModel hashed codes
findings.body: The credentialModel already contains hashed recovery codes constructed via createFromValues, but generatedCodes (raw, unhashed) is passed separately into createRecoveryCodesCredential, which re-serializes the raw codes into JSON for the user-storage case. This duplicates data between credentialModel and generatedCodes and could get out of sync if createFromValues logic changes (e.g., different hash algorithm or code transformation), silently storing different codes in user storage vs local DB storage.
